assets.statement: All BCH assigned to outstanding 0.1 BCH tickets.
The unique state lineage, exact public counters, roots, and successor authority.
Owner secrets, rho values, note indices, paths, and wallet recovery material.
The cryptographic unlinkability of a withdrawal from its funding deposit within admitted public leakage.
A note owner can reconstruct state and unilaterally withdraw without a coordinator or private operator database.
The provenance, reproducibility, and scope integrity of qualification artifacts.

adversaries.statement: Controls the wallet, witnesses, proof bytes, transaction construction, and arbitrary malformed encodings.
Observes the mempool and chain and copies or mutates honest proof-bearing transactions.
Constructs a competing valid or invalid action against the same public state tip.
Attempts to retain minting authority, substitute configuration, carrier locks, or privileged paths at genesis.
Introduces parser, arithmetic, transcript, masking, serialization, concurrency, or recovery faults without malicious intent.
Represents future cryptanalytic capability against components whose assumptions are not post-quantum.

securityGoals.statement: No accepted transition creates a spendable ticket or payout without the exact matching reserve and state transition.
Only knowledge of the private owner secret for an unspent committed note can authorize its exact ticket withdrawal.
One note yields at most one accepted nullifier insertion and payout.
Every validity-relevant source, state, carrier, payout, fee, ordering, and successor field is bound without proof/signature circularity.
Proofs reveal no note secret, owner secret, rho, private note index, or authentication path beyond the declared public statement and admitted leakage.
A wallet with its own backup material and public chain access can reconstruct and withdraw without another party's private state.
Every qualification claim is supported by pinned sources, exact artifacts, current BCH execution, and adversarial evidence of the same relation and profile.

assumptions: Current BCH consensus and standardness rules execute as pinned by the lane environment profile.
The selected 32-byte primitives satisfy their explicitly derived binding, preimage, transcript, and PQ/classical assumptions.
Wallet entropy used for owner secrets, rho, and proof masks is generated and stored correctly.
The concrete genesis audit proves unique lineage and destruction of all disallowed minting or privileged authority.
Ordinary BCH UTXO conflict resolution serializes spends of one state tip; it does not guarantee censorship resistance or confirmation timing.
admittedLeakage: Every deposit and withdrawal transaction, time, fixed 0.1 BCH amount, fee input, transparent change, and withdrawal payout are public.
Every deposit note commitment and its public insertion index, equal to the pre-state deposit count, are public; only the note preimage, owner secret, rho, and authentication path remain private.
Pool state outpoint, public deposit and withdrawal counts, roots, proof size, verifier topology, and carrier lineage are public.
The withdrawal nullifier is public and linkable to any attempted reuse of the same note.
Network identifiers, software timing, wallet broadcast behavior, and chain-level timing correlations are not hidden by the proof relation.
outOfScope: multi-user batching, private transfers, change notes, and variable amounts
censorship resistance beyond ordinary BCH propagation and mining
BCH consensus failure or a quantum-secure replacement for the BCH settlement boundary
runtime protocol migration, upgradeability, admin recovery, or privileged emergency spend

threats.scenario: A false AIR, FRI, Merkle, transcript, or final-polynomial claim is accepted.
threats.gate: Any accepted forged proof is fatal; heuristic security arithmetic is not a pass.

threats.scenario: A valid proof or action is replayed against another state tip, pool, network, or successor.
requiredControls: old outpoint and exact states in statement
threats.gate: Every replay variant rejects as a complete transaction.

threats.scenario: An honest proof is copied while payout, state, fee, source, output, sequence, or ordering is changed.
threats.gate: Any honest-proof transaction substitution acceptance is fatal.

threats.scenario: State or carrier value pays a fee, payout differs from one ticket, or counts and value diverge.
threats.gate: All single-value mutations reject and valid transactions balance exactly.

threats.scenario: A prover withdraws a member note without the committed owner secret or swaps note/path/index fields.
threats.gate: All authority and membership mutations reject.

threats.scenario: The same note is withdrawn twice because non-membership, derivation, or insertion is incomplete.
threats.gate: A previously inserted nullifier can never produce a second accepted successor.

threats.scenario: A verifier role is omitted, duplicated, cross-spliced, replaced by an accepting filler, or not recreated.
requiredControls: exact role ordering and source locks
threats.gate: Every role/lifecycle mutation rejects without a replenishment dependency.

threats.scenario: Alternate field, point, length, role, parameter, or proof encodings are interpreted differently by two components.
threats.gate: No alternate representation or trailing data is accepted.

threats.scenario: Unmasked commitments, FRI folding, reused masks, proof shape, or repeated proofs leak witness-dependent information.
threats.gate: No withdrawal candidate proceeds without an approved ZK leakage worksheet and adversarial tests.

threats.scenario: A wallet proves against a stale state, crashes mid-action, loses a race, observes eviction, or follows a reorged successor.
requiredControls: public replay plus private note backup
threats.gate: Lifecycle tests recover without accepting stale proofs or requiring private operator state.

threats.scenario: Repeated state races, mempool policy, carrier exhaustion, or proving latency prevents practical unilateral withdrawal.
requiredControls: explicit finite accumulator capacity and exhausted-deposit behavior
threats.gate: Document measured retry costs and any ordinary BCH liveness limits; no coordinator may become required.

threats.scenario: A retained minting capability or ambiguous genesis/config identity creates a confusing state clone.
requiredControls: acyclic protocol-template, pool-instance, and carrier-manifest digest derivation
downstream genesis outpoint and deployed-lock audit record
destruction of minting and privileged authority
threats.gate: No pool instance is deployable without a unique-lineage genesis artifact.

threats.scenario: A hash-oriented proof is called post-quantum while authorization, wallet storage, signatures, or BCH settlement retains classical dependencies.
threats.gate: The complete system is never labeled PQ until every relevant component independently qualifies.

threats.scenario: A Fibonacci, Goldilocks, generic Cairo, estimated-size, dirty-tree, or single-seed result is reported as qualified PoolActionFv1 evidence.
threats.gate: Any scope or provenance mismatch blocks qualification and promotion.

pqInventory.component: Circle-FRI proof soundness and zero knowledge
pqInventory.securityRole: proof of the private note and state-transition relation
pqInventory.target: At least 128-bit classical systemic soundness first, with explicit quantum-security analysis of all hash and algebraic assumptions.
pqInventory.claimPolicy: Hash use alone is not a qualification; list decoding, Fiat-Shamir, field capacity, implementation, and masking assumptions remain explicit.

pqInventory.component: note commitment, owner authorization commitment, nullifier, and accumulators
pqInventory.securityRole: private ownership, membership, uniqueness, and binding
pqInventory.target: PQ-oriented primitives with no reduction in the classical binding and preimage requirements.
pqInventory.claimPolicy: No ECDLP authorization is introduced into the private path without explicit review.

pqInventory.component: wallet entropy, storage encryption, backup, and recovery
pqInventory.securityRole: confidentiality and availability of note secrets
pqInventory.target: A component-level storage and recovery design matching the proof-path lifetime assumptions.
pqInventory.claimPolicy: Proof-system assumptions do not imply secure wallet storage.

pqInventory.securityRole: authorization of user-owned transparent BCH inputs
pqInventory.target: Current standard BCH authorization for the first implementation, disclosed as a classical boundary.
pqInventory.claimPolicy: The explicit fee input prevents a whole-system PQ claim.

pqInventory.component: BCH consensus, transaction identifiers, mining, and ordinary output authorization
pqInventory.target: Use current BCH without weakening standardness or availability; inventory future migration separately.
classicalDependencies: current BCH ecosystem authorization and settlement assumptions
pqInventory.claimPolicy: A PQ-oriented private proof path is not a post-quantum blockchain.

promotionRule: Promotion remains closed until every open blocker has concrete controls, valid and single-invariant invalid vectors, complete current-BCH execution evidence, and root/SOL review against this exact relation and profile.
